chunks: From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I asked Abā Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him) about the female slave when her master dies. He said: 'The husband of the one she is waiting for observes the waiting period of the deceased.' I said: 'If a man married her before her waiting period expired?' He said: 'He separates from her, then marries her with a new marriage contract after the expiration of the waiting period.' I said: 'Then what about what reached us from your father:
In the case of a man who marries a woman during her waiting period, she does not become permissible to him ever.
He said: 'That is a layman (who said that).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a man who marries a female slave before her master's death waiting period expires?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a female slave observes the waiting period of her master upon his death, establishing her legal status relative to his heirs. He resolves the apparent contradiction with the general prohibition of marrying a woman during her ʿiddah by distinguishing between the specific case of a slave (where the master's death triggers the ʿiddah) and a free woman, attributing the stricter, absolute view to a layman's (jahil) understanding rather than the infallible Imams. This highlights the Shia method of reconciling narrations by distinguishing between specific contexts and general principles.
